notes:
I couldn't do any of this research, so I have no notes to give you. My first attempt to use the search tool came back with an error saying I had no more search calls left for this turn. I never got to read a single page.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. If I wrote notes on Psalm 51 now, they would come from my own memory, so I haven't written any.

If you send the request again, I'll start with these pages:

- **Verse-by-verse sources:** enduringword.com, preceptaustin.org, and the commentaries by Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com and studylight.org.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
  - v. 5 (inherited sin, from Reformed, Lutheran and Wesleyan writers)
  - v. 11 (whether the Holy Spirit can be taken away, from Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan and Pentecostal writers, plus gotquestions.org)
  - vv. 16–17 (sacrifices and a broken spirit)
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org notes on the heading, vv. 4–5 and vv. 18–19, which scholars often think were added later
  - Catholic readings on newadvent.org and catholic.com, such as Augustine on the Miserere and the psalm's use in confession
  - Orthodox readings on oca.org (the psalm is Psalm 50 in their numbering and is used in daily prayers)
  - What these sites say about hyper-grace teaching on confession, if anything
